bull.b: Sustained sequential revenue growth, alongside expansion from 192 MW toward approximately 206 MW, indicates improving commercialization of the operating platform. Greater capacity and utilization can broaden recurring infrastructure revenue and support scaling across renewable-powered computing sites over the coming quarters.

Owning both generation assets and nearby compute infrastructure gives Soluna greater control over power access, site economics, and deployment timing. This vertically integrated model can strengthen its ability to offer renewable-powered capacity and retain more value as workloads shift toward AI and HPC.

The Applied Digital joint venture adds an experienced capital and development partner while advancing a defined 50 MW AI/HPC project at Dorothy 3. If closing conditions and definitive agreements are completed, the structure could accelerate Soluna’s transition toward larger, contracted digital infrastructure opportunities.

bear.b: Material negative operating and free cash flow means the business is not currently funding operations or expansion internally. Continued cash consumption increases dependence on external capital, limits flexibility during execution setbacks, and makes sustained profitability and disciplined project financing important over the next several quarters.

Gross profit compression shows that capacity growth is not yet translating proportionally into earnings, as new sites incur costs before full revenue contribution and Briscoe requires repairs. If ramp expenses persist, low margins could delay the point at which expansion produces durable operating leverage.

The planned partnership could improve project funding, but closing depends on tax, title, lease, operating-agreement, and other conditions. The potential reimbursement obligation and share warrant add financing and execution exposure, making project conversion and capital formation important risks to the growth plan.
